reason: Female-flower pedicels lengthen to 6–7(–12) mm in fruit; bearer, numbers, extreme and the 'in fruit' stage are all right.
'Racèmes: 3–7' gives the number of racemes.
'Immature berry glabrous': fruit glabrous with the immature state kept.

fix: A heading like 'Upper stem leaves' limits everything after it, up to the next part name. Carry it as a position slot on the lamina.
reason: The linear-to-spathulate shape is said only of the upper stem leaves. This Lepidium has differently shaped lower and basal leaves, so the statement is too general without the position. The shape reading itself is fine.
Leaf blade 'long-attenuate at the tip': attenuate on the lamina tip.

fix: In 'X in N row(s)', N counts the rows, not X. Read it as an arrangement (uniseriate/biseriate), not as an amount of X.
reason: The flora says the sori form one row on each side of the midrib, not that there is one sorus per side.
Flowers numerous (in the pistillate inflorescence): present, many.
Perianth green or pale pink. The 'in anthesis' stage could be added, but the statement is not false without it.
'The branches stigmatic' means the style branches carry the stigma, so a stigma is present. A weaker reading, but true.
Calyx 'lobes linéaires, de 1,5–2 mm de long'.
The compound 'elliptic-oblong' is read as a continuum on the lamina. The 'lanceolate to' part is presumably a separate annotation.

fix: When a list item starts with 'margin', the quality belongs to the margin, not the blade. Swap the bearer as for 'base'/'apex'.
reason: Serrate to dentate describes the leaf margin, not the shape of the whole lamina.
Stamens shorter than petals.

fix: 'fewer than N' is a strict bound (at most N−1); the record should mark the maximum as exclusive.
reason: Number of leaves below 10. The upper bound is exclusive, a minor point.
Young shoots glandular-hairy, with 'young' and 'usually' kept.

fix: In 'X bearing <colour> hairs', the colour belongs to the hairs, not to X.
reason: The yellowish colour is of the hairs on the peduncle-bracts, not of the bracts.

fix: 'not seen', 'unknown', 'not known' mean the author had no material. They are not absence and should be skipped.
reason: 'Fruit not seen' does not say the fruit is absent.
Filaments adnate to perianth segments (for ca. 1 mm).
Lamina surfaces glabrous or hairy.
Ovary ovoid. PATO:0001891 is the solid ovoid sense (to be relabelled 'ovoid' by the pending PATO PR); the ovary is a 3-D organ.
The lamina base is thinly woolly on its abaxial surface. The abaxial side is lost, but the statement stays true.
Bracteoles exceed the pedicels, i.e. are longer than them.

fix: In 'few–several-flowered' and similar count-word ranges, keep both ends; do not take only the first word.
reason: The flora gives a range, few to several flowers per inflorescence, but only 'few' was recorded.

fix: A size after 'Stems …' in FNA is stem length, not plant height. Use plant height only for 'Plants …' or 'herbs … tall'.
reason: 'Stems few to several, (1-)2-6(-7.5) dm' measures the stems. The unit conversion is right.
Inflorescences to 10 cm long.

fix: Qualities in the clause after 'mericarps' belong to the mericarp. A schizocarp splits, so 'fruit not dehiscent' misstates it.
reason: The mericarps are indehiscent, not the fruit (schizocarp) as a whole.
Racemes are present.
Vermilion fruit, approximately red.
Ovary adnate to the disk. Only the lower part is, but the statement is still true.
Bract apex acuminate.
